request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: This video covers changes to mileage handling in Expense Agent. Mileage rates can now have start and end dates, so a new rate for the next period can be set up ahead of time. Rates can also be set per vehicle type, such as car, truck, SUV or motorcycle. The presenter shows the setup in Expense Agent setup and then creates a mileage expense, where the user picks a vehicle type and the amount is calculated from the date. The simple standard rate model still works for companies that don't need this.

chapters.title: Intro and the old single-rate limitation
What is new: date ranges and vehicle types

features.name: Mileage rates with date ranges
features.description: Mileage allowance can now have a start and end date, and the next period's rate can be set up immediately. The system uses the previous amount until the last day of the previous period and the new amount in the next period.
caveats: Optional: if you don't need the complexity you can skip it and use the single simple rate
prerequisites: Mileage rate setup configured in Expense Agent setup

features.name: Mileage rates per vehicle type
features.description: Mileage rates can be set per period and per vehicle type (car, truck, SUV, motorcycle, or any other type). A new table holds the vehicle types, and the user picks the vehicle type when creating a mileage expense.
caveats: If vehicle types are configured, the user must choose one before an amount is calculated
If no vehicle types are configured, the system does not offer them
prerequisites: Vehicle types defined in the new vehicle type table

features.name: Standard rate of mileage (simple model)
features.description: The existing standard rate of mileage setup still works. If a standard rate is entered, the system does not use the new, more complex mileage rate setup.
caveats: The standard rate takes precedence over the mileage rate setup when it is filled in

features.name: Automatic mileage amount calculation
features.description: When creating a mileage expense, the system looks at the date and, where relevant, the chosen vehicle type, and fills in the amount to submit. In the demo, a car gave 1.25 and a truck gave 2.5 per mile.
caveats: No calculated amount appears until a vehicle type is chosen when vehicle types are configured
prerequisites: Mileage rate setup, and vehicle types if used

features.name: Optional currency code on mileage rates
features.description: The mileage rate setup has a currency code field that can be used. Most companies use local currency for mileage, so it normally does not need to be filled in.
